title: U.S. House · Illinois's 14th District
area: Western Chicago suburbs and exurbs, including parts of Kane, Kendall, DuPage, and DeKalb counties.

context.text: Incumbent Lauren Underwood ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. James Marter defeated Gary Vician and write-in candidate Krystal Dorey in the Republican primary, 74.9% to 25.0% (Dorey 0.0%).

candidates.name: Lauren Underwood
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Lauren Underwood is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 14th District, first elected in 2018. She previously worked as a nurse, professor, and senior advisor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

background.text: Born in Cuyahoga County, Ohio; graduated from Neuqua Valley High School in Naperville, Illinois.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Michigan and a master's degree from Johns Hopkins University.
Worked as a nurse, professor, and senior advisor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Committee on Appropriations (Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration and Related Agencies; Homeland Security).

candidates.name: James Marter
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 74.9% of the vote

summary.text: James Marter is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 14th Congressional District. He lives in Bartonville, Illinois and has a background as a business owner, having run for Congress in prior cycles.

background.text: Graduated from Limestone Community High School; earned a B.S. in industrial management with a minor in computer science from Purdue University.
Received professional certification from the American Production and Inventory Control Society.
Career experience as a business owner and entrepreneur.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has completed the 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey with citable statements; no campaign-website issue positions were located within the research budget for this race, so priorities and positions are not documented here.
